age-calculator.seoDescription: An Age Calculator is a free online tool that calculates your exact age from your date of birth. Unlike a simple year difference, it provides a precise breakdown in years, months, days, hours, minutes, and total weeks. It also shows the day of the week you were born, your zodiac sign, and the number of days until your next birthday. It is useful for forms, legal documents, visa applications, or satisfying your curiosity.
age-calculator.howToStep1: Select your date of birth using the date picker.
age-calculator.howToStep2: Your exact age appears instantly in years, months, and days.

age-calculator.howToStep5: Click Copy Full Report to save or share your results.
age-calculator.faq1Answer: Age is calculated by finding the difference between today's date and your date of birth. The tool accounts for leap years and varying month lengths to provide an exact breakdown in years, months, and days.
age-calculator.faq2Question: What is the difference between chronological and biological age?
age-calculator.faq2Answer: Chronological age is the actual time elapsed since you were born, which is what this calculator measures. Biological age reflects how old your body appears based on health markers and can differ from chronological age.
age-calculator.faq3Answer: No. All calculations happen entirely in your browser. Your birthdate is not sent to a server or stored by this calculator.
age-calculator.faq4Question: Can I use this for official documents?
age-calculator.faq4Answer: The results provide a mathematical age calculation and may help you complete visa applications, school forms, medical paperwork, and other documents requiring your age. Always follow the specific requirements of the relevant authority.

curlToFetch.title: cURL to Fetch & Axios Converter
curlToFetch.subtitle: Translate cURL commands into idiomatic JavaScript fetch() and Axios HTTP requests instantly.
curlToFetch.aboutText: The cURL to Fetch & Axios Converter is a browser-based developer utility that deconstructs raw cURL terminal commands and translates them into modern, production-ready JavaScript code. It parses HTTP methods (-X, --request), headers (-H), basic and bearer authentication (-u, --user), query parameters, URL-encoded forms, and JSON payloads (--data, -d, --data-raw). The tool outputs clean Fetch API promises using async/await and Axios request configurations ready for frontend or Node.js applications.
curlToFetch.feature1: Comprehensive cURL Syntax Parsing: Accurately handles headers, query params, cookies, basic auth, and multipart form-data
curlToFetch.feature2: Dual Modern Output Formats: Instantly toggle between browser-native Fetch API (async/await) and Axios client syntax
curlToFetch.feature3: Zero Server Transmission: Command parsing and code generation execute entirely in browser memory for complete credential safety
curlToFetch.feature4: Production-Ready Formatting: Generates clean, properly indented, error-handled JavaScript snippets with one-click copy
curlToFetch.step1Body: Copy a cURL command from your terminal, API documentation, or browser DevTools Network tab and paste it into the editor.
curlToFetch.step2Body: Switch between native browser Fetch and Axios tabs to compare syntax and request structure.
curlToFetch.step3Body: Review the formatted JavaScript code, then click "Copy" to import the request snippet directly into your codebase.
curlToFetch.faq1Q: Which cURL flags and options are supported?
curlToFetch.faq1A: The parser handles primary HTTP flags including -X/--request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH), -H/--header, -d/--data/--data-raw (JSON and form data), -u/--user (Basic Auth), and URL parameters.
curlToFetch.faq2Q: Does this converter upload sensitive API tokens or passwords?
curlToFetch.faq2A: No. The entire conversion logic executes client-side in your browser using pure JavaScript parsing. No commands or authorization headers are sent to remote servers.
curlToFetch.faq3Q: Does the generated Fetch code support error handling?
curlToFetch.faq3A: Yes, generated Fetch examples demonstrate standard HTTP response status validation (res.ok) and asynchronous JSON body resolution.
curlToFetch.faq4Q: Can I convert commands exported from Chrome or Firefox DevTools?
curlToFetch.faq4A: Yes. Right-click any network request in Chrome, Firefox, or Safari, select "Copy as cURL", and paste it directly into this tool.

curlToPython.title: cURL to Python Requests Converter
curlToPython.subtitle: Transform cURL terminal commands into idiomatic Python requests code instantly with zero latency.
curlToPython.aboutText: The cURL to Python Requests Converter converts command-line cURL commands into clean, idiomatic Python code utilizing the widely-used requests library. It intelligently parses HTTP request methods, custom headers, cookies, URL parameters, basic authentication credentials, and data payloads (both application/json and form-encoded data). Ideal for data engineers, backend developers, and automation specialists converting API documentation into maintainable Python scripts.
curlToPython.feature1: Idiomatic Python Output: Formats payloads as Python dictionaries, preserving types, nested keys, and custom headers
curlToPython.feature2: Smart Auth & Payload Detection: Automatically maps -u flags to requests.auth.HTTPBasicAuth and JSON payloads to json=
curlToPython.feature3: 100% In-Browser Privacy: API keys, bearer tokens, and confidential request bodies never leave your local browser environment
curlToPython.feature4: Instant Syntax Highlighting: Clean Python code structure formatted according to PEP 8 standards with rapid copy support
curlToPython.step1Body: Paste your raw cURL command into the input editor; line continuations (\) are parsed automatically.
curlToPython.step2Body: Inspect the generated headers dictionary, params map, auth tuple, and requests invocation.
curlToPython.step3Body: Click "Copy Code" to paste the snippet into your Jupyter notebook, FastAPI service, or automation script.
curlToPython.faq1Q: Does this tool use Python requests or httpx?
curlToPython.faq1A: It generates standard Python requests code with clean dictionaries for headers, params, and JSON data. The resulting syntax is easily adaptable to httpx as well.
curlToPython.faq2Q: How are JSON bodies formatted in Python?
curlToPython.faq2A: If the cURL command contains valid JSON data in -d or --data-raw, it is converted into a native Python dictionary passed to the json= parameter.
curlToPython.faq3Q: Are sensitive authorization headers leaked during conversion?
curlToPython.faq3A: Never. All tokenization, parsing, and code synthesis take place exclusively in client-side memory without network transmissions.
curlToPython.faq4Q: How does it handle multiline cURL commands?
curlToPython.faq4A: The parser automatically strips backslash line continuations (\) and normalizes whitespace before analyzing flags and arguments.

discountCalculator.title: Discount & Sale Price Calculator
discountCalculator.subtitle: Calculate retail sale prices, customer savings, stacked percentage discounts, and original pre-sale prices.
discountCalculator.aboutText: The Discount & Sale Price Calculator is an indispensable retail and financial planning tool designed to compute exact savings, post-discount prices, and multi-tier stacked discounts. It supports three distinct modes: finding the sale price given a discount percentage, reverse-engineering the original price from a discounted price tag, and calculating stacked promotional discounts (e.g., 20% off plus an extra 15% clearance). All calculations display effective net savings without rounding discrepancies.
discountCalculator.feature1: Three Calculation Modes: Calculate sale price, reverse-engineer original price, or evaluate stacked discounts
discountCalculator.feature2: Accurate Multi-Tier Stacking: Correctly calculates sequential discounts applied to reduced balances rather than misleading simple sums
discountCalculator.feature3: Dynamic Real-Time Breakdown: Instantly view monetary amount saved, final customer payable amount, and effective discount rate
discountCalculator.feature4: International Currency Formatting: Seamlessly adapts currency symbols and numeric separators according to the active locale
discountCalculator.step1Body: Choose "Find Sale Price", "Find Original Price", or "Stacked Discounts" depending on your retail scenario.
discountCalculator.step2Body: Input the original amount, discounted price, or sequential discount percentages.
discountCalculator.step3Body: Inspect your total monetary savings and effective percentage, then click "Copy Breakdown".
discountCalculator.faq1Q: How do stacked discounts actually work?
discountCalculator.faq1A: Stacked discounts are applied sequentially. For example, a 20% discount followed by an additional 10% discount results in an effective 28% total discount, not 30%, because the second discount applies to the already discounted price.
discountCalculator.faq2Q: Can I find the original price if I only know what I paid?
discountCalculator.faq2A: Yes. Switch to "Find Original Price", enter the final amount paid and the discount rate applied, and the tool will calculate the pre-discount sticker price.
discountCalculator.faq3Q: Does this calculator support decimals and tax?
discountCalculator.faq3A: Yes, you can enter fractional currency values (e.g. 19.99). You can also apply tax percentages by compounding or adjusting the baseline price.
discountCalculator.faq4Q: Is any financial data stored or uploaded?
discountCalculator.faq4A: No. All calculations are executed locally in your browser session and are never logged or transmitted.

gradeCalculator.title: Weighted Grade & Final Exam Calculator
gradeCalculator.subtitle: Calculate weighted course grades, letter grades, GPA, and determine required final exam scores.
gradeCalculator.aboutText: The Weighted Grade & Final Exam Calculator enables students, educators, and academic advisors to determine accurate cumulative course grades based on weighted syllabus categories. With support for assignments, midterms, quizzes, and projects, the tool computes weighted percentage averages, standard letter grade equivalents, and 4.0 scale GPA conversions. Its built-in "What-If" final exam calculator reveals the exact score needed on remaining coursework to secure a desired target grade.
gradeCalculator.feature1: Flexible Weighted Categories: Add unlimited assignments, homework, labs, and exams with individual percentage weights
gradeCalculator.feature2: What-If Final Exam Projection: Automatically calculates the exact exam grade required to earn an A, B, or custom target percentage
gradeCalculator.feature3: Letter Grade & GPA Mapping: Automatically converts numerical averages into standard academic letter grades and 4.0 scale GPA
gradeCalculator.feature4: Validation & Summary Export: Visual validation flags when total category weight exceeds 100%, with easy one-click summary copying
gradeCalculator.step1Body: Input your scores and syllabus weights for each completed coursework component.
gradeCalculator.step2Body: In the "What-If" section, specify your desired final course grade percentage.
gradeCalculator.step3Body: See your current standing and the score required on remaining exams, then copy your full grade summary.
gradeCalculator.faq1A: In a weighted grading system, each assignment category contributes a fixed percentage to your final course grade. Each category's percentage score is multiplied by its weight, and the products are summed.
gradeCalculator.faq2Q: What happens if total weight does not equal 100%?
gradeCalculator.faq2A: The calculator displays your current standing based on the weights completed so far, and shows the remaining percentage allocated to upcoming exams.
gradeCalculator.faq3Q: How does the What-If calculator determine my needed exam score?
gradeCalculator.faq3A: It uses the formula: Needed Score = (Desired Grade - Current Weighted Points) / Remaining Weight, identifying whether your goal is realistic or mathematically impossible.
gradeCalculator.faq4Q: Are my grades stored on any server?
gradeCalculator.faq4A: No. All calculations run strictly in your browser session; no academic records or grades are uploaded or stored.

hashGenerator.title: Cryptographic Hash Generator (SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5)
hashGenerator.subtitle: Generate SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5 cryptographic hashes instantly with client-side security.
hashGenerator.aboutText: The Cryptographic Hash Generator is a high-performance, browser-based security utility for producing deterministic, one-way hash digests from arbitrary text or binary data. Supporting standard cryptographic hashing algorithms—including SHA-256, SHA-512, and legacy MD5—the tool operates directly within browser memory. It is widely used by cybersecurity engineers, developers, and system administrators for file integrity validation, password hashing analysis, and digital signature verification.
hashGenerator.feature1: Multi-Algorithm Simultaneous Hashing: Computes SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5 digests concurrently in real time as you type
hashGenerator.feature2: 100% Client-Side Cryptography: Operates completely offline in local memory without transmitting sensitive text to external servers
hashGenerator.feature3: Cryptographic Standard Compliance: Adheres strictly to NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA family) and RFC 1321 (MD5) specifications
hashGenerator.feature4: One-Click Hash Export: Clean hexadecimal lowercase digests with convenient one-click copy buttons for rapid clipboard transfer
hashGenerator.step1Body: Type or paste your secret string, token, or data payload into the input editor.
hashGenerator.step2Body: Review the computed hexadecimal hash digests across MD5 (128-bit), SHA-256 (256-bit), and SHA-512 (512-bit).
hashGenerator.step3Body: Click "Copy" next to the target hash algorithm to save the digest string to your clipboard.
hashGenerator.faq1Q: Can a cryptographic hash be decrypted back to the original text?
hashGenerator.faq1A: No. Cryptographic hashes are one-way mathematical functions. You cannot reverse or decrypt a hash digest back into plaintext; you can only verify matches by hashing candidate inputs.
hashGenerator.faq2Q: What is the difference between SHA-256 and MD5?
hashGenerator.faq2A: MD5 produces a 128-bit digest and is cryptographically broken due to known collision vulnerabilities, used primarily for legacy checksums. SHA-256 produces a collision-resistant 256-bit digest recommended for modern security standards.
hashGenerator.faq3Q: Is this hash generator safe for sensitive passwords and API keys?
hashGenerator.faq3A: Yes. All hashing algorithms run 100% client-side inside your browser engine. Zero input characters or hashes are ever sent over the internet.
hashGenerator.faq4Q: Does case sensitivity affect the generated hash?
hashGenerator.faq4A: Yes. Cryptographic hash functions exhibit the avalanche effect: even changing a single character or its case produces a completely different hash digest.

hmacGenerator.title: HMAC Signature Generator
hmacGenerator.subtitle: Generate secure Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, HMAC-MD5) instantly.
hmacGenerator.aboutText: The HMAC Signature Generator is a specialized cryptographic utility designed to compute Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC) compliant with RFC 2104 and FIPS PUB 198. By combining a shared secret cryptographic key with a message payload through an underlying hash function (SHA-256, SHA-512, or MD5), HMAC guarantees both data integrity and authenticity. It is essential for signing REST API requests (e.g., AWS Signature Version 4, Stripe webhooks, GitHub webhooks) and verifying message authenticity.
hmacGenerator.feature1: Standard Algorithm Selection: Supports HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, and HMAC-MD5 with exact cryptographic adherence
hmacGenerator.feature2: Client-Side Key Isolation: Shared secret keys and private messages are processed strictly in browser memory, never sent over the network
hmacGenerator.feature3: Real-Time Live Calculation: Automatically recalculates signatures immediately upon modifying either the key, message, or algorithm
hmacGenerator.feature4: Hexadecimal Digest Formatting: Produces standardized lowercase hexadecimal signature strings ready for HTTP header authorization
hmacGenerator.step1Body: Input your shared secret key or API signing secret into the designated key field.
hmacGenerator.step2Body: Choose HMAC-SHA256, SHA-512, or MD5, and paste your JSON payload or request string.
hmacGenerator.step3Body: Review the resulting hexadecimal HMAC signature and click "Copy" to use in your API headers.
hmacGenerator.faq1Q: What is an HMAC and how does it differ from a regular hash?
hmacGenerator.faq1A: A standard hash (like SHA-256) only verifies data integrity. An HMAC incorporates a secret cryptographic key, ensuring both data integrity and proof that the message originated from a party holding the secret key.
hmacGenerator.faq2Q: Is my secret key safe when using this tool?
hmacGenerator.faq2A: Yes, completely. All cryptographic operations are executed locally in your browser using client-side JavaScript. Your secret key and message payload are never transmitted to any external server.
hmacGenerator.faq3Q: Which HMAC algorithm should I choose for modern webhooks?
hmacGenerator.faq3A: HMAC-SHA256 is the industry standard for modern webhooks (used by GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, and Slack) offering high performance and robust security.
hmacGenerator.faq4Q: Can HMAC signatures prevent replay attacks?
hmacGenerator.faq4A: HMAC itself verifies message authenticity. To prevent replay attacks, webhooks commonly include a timestamp in the signed payload and verify it against a short validity window.

htmlEncoderDecoder.title: HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder
htmlEncoderDecoder.subtitle: Convert special characters into HTML entities or decode entities back to plaintext instantly.
htmlEncoderDecoder.aboutText: The HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder is a developer utility that converts reserved characters, symbols, and Unicode glyphs into standardized HTML entities (e.g., <, >, &) and decodes encoded markup back into readable text. Essential for preventing Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities, displaying raw code snippets inside HTML documents, and debugging encoded web content, this tool processes text in real time entirely within your browser.
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature1: Bi-Directional Conversion: Seamlessly toggle between Encode (Text to HTML Entities) and Decode (Entities to Plaintext)
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature2: Comprehensive Character Mapping: Safely encodes reserved characters (<, >, &, ", ') as well as high-order Unicode symbols
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature3: XSS Mitigation Support: Prepares user input strings for safe inclusion within HTML markup and templates
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature4: Zero Server Processing: All string parsing and entity conversions execute client-side for maximum speed and data privacy
htmlEncoderDecoder.step1Body: Choose "Encode" to convert special characters into entities, or "Decode" to restore entities to text.
htmlEncoderDecoder.step2Body: Paste your HTML snippet, code block, or entity-encoded string into the input panel.
htmlEncoderDecoder.step3Body: Review the converted output in the preview panel and click "Copy" to save to your clipboard.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq1Q: Why is HTML entity encoding important?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq1A: In HTML, characters like <, >, and & have structural syntactic meaning. If untrusted input containing these characters is inserted directly into a page without encoding, browsers may execute malicious scripts, resulting in XSS vulnerabilities.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2Q: What are the most common HTML entities?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2A: The five core XML/HTML entities are: < (<), > (>), & (&), " ("), and ' (').
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq3Q: Does this tool decode named entities as well as numeric entities?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq3A: Yes. It decodes named entities (such as © and  ) as well as decimal (©) and hexadecimal (©) numeric character references.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq4Q: Is my HTML data sent to a backend server?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq4A: No. All encoding and decoding operations take place in your browser memory using native DOM parser APIs, ensuring complete confidentiality.

httpHeaderInspector.title: HTTP Header Inspector & Parser
httpHeaderInspector.subtitle: Deconstruct raw HTTP request or response headers into structured key-value maps with security analysis.
httpHeaderInspector.aboutText: The HTTP Header Inspector & Parser is an essential networking and web security tool that parses raw HTTP request and response headers into clear, structured key-value tables. It automatically identifies core networking parameters (Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Accept-Encoding), detects caching directives (Cache-Control, ETag, Age), and highlights critical security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options). Perfect for debugging API responses and validating web server security configurations.
httpHeaderInspector.feature1: Instant Raw Header Parsing: Automatically strips status lines and tokenizes multiline headers into structured key-value pairs
httpHeaderInspector.feature2: Security Header Identification: Highlights presence and values of vital defense-in-depth headers like CSP, HSTS, and CORS
httpHeaderInspector.feature3: Clean JSON & Table Export: Formats parsed headers into accessible tables with single-click JSON clipboard export
httpHeaderInspector.feature4: 100% Private Client Analysis: No network requests are made; analysis occurs entirely in browser memory on pasted text
httpHeaderInspector.step1Body: Copy raw response headers from curl, Postman, or your browser DevTools Network tab and paste them in.
httpHeaderInspector.step2Body: Review the parsed headers categorized by standard protocol, caching, and security attributes.
httpHeaderInspector.step3Body: Click "Copy" to export the parsed header object as formatted JSON for use in automated tests or reports.
httpHeaderInspector.faq1Q: What headers are most critical for web application security?
httpHeaderInspector.faq1A: Key security headers include Content-Security-Policy (CSP) to mitigate XSS, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) to enforce HTTPS, X-Frame-Options to block clickjacking, and X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME-sniffing.
httpHeaderInspector.faq2Q: Can I parse both HTTP request and response headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq2A: Yes. The parser recognizes both request headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, Accept) and response headers (e.g., Set-Cookie, Cache-Control, Server).
httpHeaderInspector.faq3Q: How does it handle duplicate headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq3A: Per RFC 7230, headers with duplicate field names (such as Set-Cookie or Accept) are properly preserved and grouped rather than overwritten.
httpHeaderInspector.faq4Q: Does this tool inspect headers over live network connections?
httpHeaderInspector.faq4A: This tool is an offline parser designed for analyzing pasted header blocks without sending outbound HTTP probes, ensuring maximum security and zero firewall restrictions.

invoiceGenerator.title: Free Invoice Generator
invoiceGenerator.subtitle: Create professional invoices in seconds — download as PDF, multi-currency support, zero limits.
invoiceGenerator.aboutText: The Free Invoice Generator is a comprehensive, client-side business billing tool that lets freelancers, contractors, and small businesses create polished, professional invoices directly in their browser. Featuring multi-item line item calculation, customizable tax rates, discount percentages, shipping fees, payment terms, and notes, it compiles invoices instantly with live visual preview and one-click PDF generation. No account registration, subscriptions, or server storage required.
invoiceGenerator.feature1: Dynamic Line Item Math: Automatically computes row totals, subtotals, tax amounts, applied discounts, and net balance due
invoiceGenerator.feature2: Global Currency Support: Customize currency symbols (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, INR, etc.) and locale formatting seamlessly
invoiceGenerator.feature3: Instant PDF Export: Generate clean, print-ready vector PDF invoices directly from browser memory without watermarks
invoiceGenerator.feature4: Complete Data Privacy: Client names, addresses, item costs, and financial figures are never saved on remote servers
invoiceGenerator.step1Body: Fill in your business name, contact information, invoice number, issue date, and due date.
invoiceGenerator.step2Body: List products or services with quantities and unit rates; configure applicable tax rates and discounts.
invoiceGenerator.step3Body: Review the formatted invoice in the live preview and click "Download PDF" to deliver to your client.
invoiceGenerator.faq1Q: Is this invoice generator really completely free?
invoiceGenerator.faq1A: Yes, 100% free with no monthly limits, no watermarks, and no sign-up or credit card required.
invoiceGenerator.faq2Q: Are my clients' personal details or rates stored on your server?
invoiceGenerator.faq2A: No. All invoice information is handled exclusively within your browser's local memory. None of your business data or client invoices are transmitted or saved remotely.
invoiceGenerator.faq3Q: Can I customize the currency symbol?
invoiceGenerator.faq3A: Yes. You can select standard currencies like $, €, £, ¥, ₹, or enter any custom currency abbreviation.
invoiceGenerator.faq4Q: How do I print or email the generated invoice?
invoiceGenerator.faq4A: Click "Download PDF" to save a clean PDF document onto your computer, which you can then print or attach to an email.

jsonToGoStruct.title: JSON to Go Struct Generator
jsonToGoStruct.subtitle: Convert JSON payloads into idiomatic Go struct definitions with json tags and nested types instantly.
jsonToGoStruct.aboutText: The JSON to Go Struct Generator is an essential developer tool for Golang engineers that automatically analyzes JSON payloads and generates clean, idiomatic Go struct definitions. It correctly resolves primitive data types (string, int64, float64, bool), infers nested struct models, handles slices and arrays, accommodates nullable values with pointers or interface{}, and generates canonical struct tags (`json:"key_name"`). Designed for rapid API development and microservice modeling.
jsonToGoStruct.feature1: Idiomatic Go Naming: Converts snake_case and camelCase JSON keys into exported PascalCase Go struct field names
jsonToGoStruct.feature2: Automatic Type Inference: Accurately differentiates integers, floating-point numbers, booleans, strings, and slice types
jsonToGoStruct.feature3: Nested Struct Extraction: Decomposes deeply nested JSON objects into modular, reusable sub-struct definitions
jsonToGoStruct.feature4: Private In-Browser Generation: Generates Go source code in browser memory without transmitting API payloads over the network
jsonToGoStruct.step1Body: Paste a representative JSON API response or data object into the left editor.
jsonToGoStruct.step2Body: Specify your root struct name (e.g., UserResponse) and review field tag mappings.
jsonToGoStruct.step3Body: Click "Copy" to paste the generated Go struct definitions directly into your .go source file.
jsonToGoStruct.faq1Q: How are nested JSON objects handled?
jsonToGoStruct.faq1A: The generator creates independent, named Go sub-structs for nested JSON objects, ensuring clean, modular, and readable Go code.
jsonToGoStruct.faq2Q: Does it handle null values and empty arrays?
jsonToGoStruct.faq2A: Yes. Nullable properties are typed safely using pointers or interface{} to prevent JSON unmarshaling panics.
jsonToGoStruct.faq3Q: Are json struct tags automatically added?
jsonToGoStruct.faq3A: Yes. Every struct field includes the standard `json:"key"` tag matching the exact casing of the original JSON key.
jsonToGoStruct.faq4Q: Is my proprietary JSON schema uploaded to any server?
jsonToGoStruct.faq4A: No. All parsing, type inference, and Go code synthesis occur strictly in client-side JavaScript within your browser.

jsonToPydantic.title: JSON to Pydantic & Python Dataclass Generator
jsonToPydantic.subtitle: Generate modern Pydantic V2 models and standard Python dataclasses from JSON objects instantly.
jsonToPydantic.aboutText: The JSON to Pydantic & Python Dataclass Generator converts arbitrary JSON data structures into strongly-typed Python schemas. Supporting both Pydantic V2 (BaseModel) and standard Python 3.10+ dataclasses, it automatically infers primitive types (str, int, float, bool), creates nested model classes, handles Optional fields and List typing, and generates Field(alias="...") definitions for non-Pythonic keys. Ideal for building FastAPI endpoints, data pipelines, and SDKs.
jsonToPydantic.feature1: Dual Schema Generation: Seamlessly toggle between Pydantic V2 BaseModel syntax and native standard-library @dataclass
jsonToPydantic.feature2: Pythonic Naming & Aliasing: Converts camelCase keys to snake_case attributes with automated Pydantic Field(alias=...) support
jsonToPydantic.feature3: Type Hints & Optional Support: Generates modern PEP 484/604 type annotations including List[T] and Optional[T]
jsonToPydantic.feature4: Zero Server Exposure: Payload parsing and Python code generation run 100% locally in browser memory
jsonToPydantic.step1Body: Paste your JSON sample payload or API response into the input editor.
jsonToPydantic.step2Body: Select either Pydantic V2 BaseModel or standard Python Dataclass format.
jsonToPydantic.step3Body: Review the generated Python code and click "Copy" to import into your FastAPI or Python application.
jsonToPydantic.faq1Q: Does this generator produce Pydantic V1 or V2 syntax?
jsonToPydantic.faq1A: It generates modern Pydantic V2 syntax using BaseModel and standard typing, compatible with the latest FastAPI releases.
jsonToPydantic.faq2Q: How does it handle JSON keys with dashes or reserved keywords?
jsonToPydantic.faq2A: Keys containing dashes, numbers, or Python reserved words (such as from, class, def) are assigned sanitized attribute names with Field(alias="...") mappings.
jsonToPydantic.faq3Q: Are nested objects converted into separate models?
jsonToPydantic.faq3A: Yes. Deeply nested objects are recursively parsed into distinct model classes defined above the parent model to ensure clean Python imports.
jsonToPydantic.faq4Q: Is my JSON payload kept confidential?
jsonToPydantic.faq4A: Yes. The entire code generation logic executes locally in your browser without transmitting any payload data to external servers.

jsonToTypescript.title: JSON to TypeScript Interface Generator
jsonToTypescript.subtitle: Convert JSON objects into strongly-typed TypeScript interfaces and type aliases instantly.
jsonToTypescript.aboutText: The JSON to TypeScript Interface Generator is an essential tool for frontend and full-stack developers that converts JSON data payloads into clean, strongly-typed TypeScript interfaces. It automatically parses scalar values, infers union types, resolves arrays of objects, decomposes nested structures into individual modular interfaces, and marks nullable fields as optional. Built to streamline TypeScript development across React, Next.js, Vue, Node.js, and API integrations.
jsonToTypescript.feature1: Recursive Interface Extraction: Breaks down complex nested JSON hierarchies into discrete, reusable TypeScript interfaces
jsonToTypescript.feature2: Precise Type Inference: Accurately differentiates string, number, boolean, Array<T>, and Record<string, T> types
jsonToTypescript.feature3: Safe Optional & Union Detection: Detects null and missing attributes across array elements to generate optional properties (key?: type)
jsonToTypescript.feature4: Fast Client-Side Execution: Generates ready-to-use TypeScript definitions instantly in browser memory with zero network latency
jsonToTypescript.step1Body: Paste your JSON sample or API response into the source code editor.
jsonToTypescript.step2Body: Review the generated TypeScript interfaces and inferred property types in real time.
jsonToTypescript.step3Body: Click "Copy" to paste the interfaces directly into your .ts or .d.ts type definition files.
jsonToTypescript.faq1A: When an array contains multiple element types (e.g., numbers and strings), the generator infers a union type like Array<string | number>.
jsonToTypescript.faq2Q: Are nested JSON objects represented as separate interfaces?
jsonToTypescript.faq2A: Yes. Instead of unreadable inline type literals, each nested object is extracted into its own named, PascalCase TypeScript interface.
jsonToTypescript.faq3A: Yes. Properties that evaluate to null or are missing across items in an array are marked with the optional modifier (?).
jsonToTypescript.faq4Q: Is any of my JSON data transmitted across the web?
jsonToTypescript.faq4A: No. All JSON parsing and TypeScript type generation run 100% client-side in your browser.
